messages.content:
Risk: Harmful code generation
Description: Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems.
Concern: The execution of harmful code might open vulnerabilities in IT systems.
Policy: Operational Security & Critical Infrastructure

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts. [found by 7/10 queries]
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HarmfulHowTo: Harmful How-To — Step-by-step instructions for activities that cause property destruction, physical harm, or enable illegal intrusion when executed by unauthorized individuals. [found by 6/10 queries]
  Siblings: CBRN Information, Drug Synthesis, Dual-Use Research Concern
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#ContentSafetyHazard: Content Safety Hazard — Root class for content safety harm categories relevant to adversarial prompt generation against LLM deployments. [found by 6/10 queries]
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Cyberterrorism: Cyberterrorism — Use of digital attacks against critical infrastructure or information systems to create fear and disruption for political ends. [found by 4/10 queries]
  Siblings: International Terrorism, Domestic Terrorism
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#SabotageInstructions: Sabotage Instructions — Methods for disabling, damaging, or destroying infrastructure, equipment, or systems to cause operational disruption or economic harm. [found by 4/10 queries]
  Siblings: Arson Methods, Lock Picking and Bypassing

axes.rationale: The harmful code generated by the model can be considered dangerous information that, when executed, can cause harm or unintentionally affect other systems.
The execution of harmful code might open vulnerabilities in IT systems, which could be exploited in cyberterrorism attacks, creating fear and disruption for political ends.
